catalog_quote: 2.1 Syllabic structure The vocabulary of Arem has monosyllables and sesqui-syllables. monosyllable: C V (C) sesqui-syllable: C-C V (C) A sesqui-syllable is composed of a main syllable C V (C) preceded by a pre-syllable C-. The main syllable is identical to a monosyllable. The pre-syllable is short and unstressed, without distinctive vowel, and its consonantal system is reduced. A pre-syllable can not exist alone. ... 2.2 Voice-type register system of Arem: - Arem has two sets of vowels: Series 1 with a high-clear register phonation; Series 2, with a low-breathy register phonation (indicated by the grave accent). ... - Syllables in voiced finals show a contrast between a modal tone and a glottalized tone: in series 1 /a~aˀ/, and in series 2 /à~àˀ/. sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: 'Monosyllabic words were preferred; otherwise, I chose target syllables which were the final stressed syllables of disyllabic words.' Instrumental study of register/phonation (5 speakers, 2019/2021); no further word-stress analysis.
sources.note: Only instrumental study of Arem; confirms in passing that the final syllable of disyllables is the stressed one (p.130). downloaded now.

sources.citation: Ta, Tan (Tạ Thành Tấn). 2023. Register and Tone Developments in Vietic Languages. PhD dissertation, University of Ottawa. 480 pp. hdl:10393/44893, doi:10.20381/ruor-29099.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: p.137: 'Arem has monosyllabic and sesquisyllabic words, with the latter type accounting for 55-60% of its lexicon ... Monosyllable: C1(C2)V(C3); Sesquisyllable: CpVp.C1V(C3)'. p.138: 'The presyllable is unstressed and unmarked for tonation. ... These vowels can be reduced to a schwa in normal speech.' p.138: 'Monosyllabic words and the main syllable of sesquisyllabic words can contain the full range of onsets, vowels, and codas. They are stressed and carry a register distinction'.
sources.locator: ch.4 'Arem', sec. 4.1.2.1-4.1.2.3, pp.137-138 (also p.130 on Proto-Vietic 'iambic stress of the sesquisyllabic structure')
sources.note: Largest and newest description of Arem phonology with own fieldwork (2019, 2021) and acoustic data; its Arem sketch (pp.137-138) independently states presyllable unstressed / main syllable stressed, corroborating the Ferlus-based '01' coding. downloaded now.
